en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep rural babies warm without electricity.
The carabao, our national animal, wallows in mud to cool down because it lacks functional sweat glands.
Local government units enforce the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and prevent dengue.
Street dancers in the Sinulog festival must wear bright clothing at night so drivers can see them and avoid accidents.
The Ifugao built rice terraces with stone walls that prevent soil erosion and filter water for safe irrigation.
Filipino parents fulfill their duty to protect children by bringing them to barangay health centers for free immunizations.
The sampaguita, our national flower, contains natural compounds that traditional healers use to relieve headaches and reduce fever.
Dr. Ramon Barba invented a simple flower induction technique for mangoes that increases fruit production and improves national food security.
During World War II, Filipinos survived food shortages by eating vitamin-rich root crops like camote that grow safely underground.
The Filipino value of bayanihan inspires community pantries during health crises to ensure neighbors share nutritious food and prevent malnutrition.
The giant lanterns of San Fernando use parallel wiring so that if one bulb breaks, the rest stay lit to prevent darkness.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees every child's right to health, ensuring access to clean drinking water and proper sanitation.
